title: My Role Model Pins Tren (A Jack Hanma Analysis)
summary: A philosophical essay using Baki's Jack Hanma as a cautionary role model for why men turn to PEDs: trauma, isolation, revenge, body dysmorphia and life-denying nihilism. Contrasting Jack with Baki, NH argues healthy masculinity is community-driven, the PED mindset is self-justifying, and gratitude for a healthy body is the antidote.
claims: Pretending PED temptations don't exist is counterproductive; understand the reasons logically so you can resist when the opportunity comes
He has been tempted by PEDs in the past
Most people take drugs, steroids included, to fill a void (unhappiness, trauma, low confidence); it's never only about muscles
The best way to reduce steroid use is not banning it but creating environments where people have no reason to take drugs
Taking revenge on whoever hurt you does not undo your own trauma
Men who claim they can't build muscle usually have bad methods, not bad bodies; true non-responders are extremely rare
Hardgainers who jump on TRT then use the results as proof they needed drugs; it only proves drugs make bad methods work
Overtraining is really under-recovering; a skinny weak lifter with low work capacity who under-eats can overtrain easily, while someone with on-point recovery barely can
Recovery periods can matter more than training if training is too dense and intense
Body dysmorphia drives overly aggressive methods that stall progress, which deepens the dysmorphia: a downward spiral
His own spiral was bulking: as a small kid obsessed with size he kept going up in weight and the dysmorphia worsened the bigger he got
Meeting dysmorphia's demands never ends it, like paying a blackmailer; the standard keeps rising like chasing the dragon
Taking drugs to fix dysmorphia is the worst option because it feeds the disorder faster
Desire can never be quenched; the wise man feeds desires moderately and chooses which to starve
People who downplay body dysmorphic disorder are wrong; he has dealt with a mild version himself
There is no such thing as one cycle; PED users he talked to all say you can never go back to training natural once you've felt it
Humans cannot go back down on a standard, so never establish an unnatural standard you can't reach without drugs
In Baki, Jack is the only PED user while Yujiro, Oliva and Doppo are natural; Baki trains in 25-30% of his panels, environmental storytelling that training alone is the right way
Amor fati: accept life's hardships without becoming cruel; becoming a bully after being bullied lets the bullies win
Rejecting bad genetics by injecting PEDs is 'odium fati', a life-denying rejection of one's fate that fixes nothing and creates lifelong dependence
Healthy masculinity is community-driven; strength is for others, and the lone-wolf trope is pathological
PED users rarely face that they are shortening their lives; bravado serves as a front that young men mistake for confidence
PED communities invent in-group morality, e.g. calling naturals weak for not 'doing whatever it takes'
Bodybuilding went from life-affirming natural bodybuilding to a life-denying death cult where pros die around 40
People follow morality only until it clashes with desire, then build a new morality to justify giving in
The Übermensch is beyond good and evil: making your own code can lead to good or evil; Baki and Jack both do it with opposite outcomes
Your circumstances don't matter in the end: you are responsible for your own happiness and future
The antidote to life-denying behavior is gratitude for being born in a sound, healthy body
